title: Record rejection reasons under the namespace declared for that role
description:
`jit issue reject --reason` writes a `resolution:<reason>` label whatever the repository declares. The reason must land in the namespace the repository declares for that role, and a repository declaring none must be refused instead of receiving an undeclared label.

## Background

- `labels::resolution_label` (`crates/jit/src/labels.rs`) formats the literal `resolution:{reason}`. `IssueOps::reject_issue` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs`) calls it and `CapturedFieldUpdate::rejection` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`) appends the label, bypassing rule enforcement.
- The `resolution` namespace is a profile declaration: the shipped `jit-default` profile contributes it as a `namespaces` map entry (`profiles/jit-default/manifest.toml`), and this repository declares it in `.jit/config.toml`. A neutral `jit init` declares no namespace at all.
- `NamespaceConfig` (`crates/jit/src/config.rs`, `[namespaces.<ns>]`, `deny_unknown_fields`) carries `description`, `unique` and `examples`; profiles contribute whole namespace entries, so a field on the entry travels with the profile without new profile mechanism.
- The `--reason` help text in `crates/jit/src/cli.rs` and the reject documentation (`docs/reference/cli-commands.md`, `docs/concepts/core-model.md`, `docs/reference/labels.md`) state the `resolution:` label as fixed behaviour.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A namespace declaration accepts an optional `role` field whose vocabulary is one semantic type with the single value `rejection-reason`; an unknown role value is a configuration parse error naming the accepted values.
- [hard] REQ-02: Rejecting with a reason in a repository where exactly one namespace declares `role = "rejection-reason"` records the label `<that-namespace>:<reason>`; a test over a repository declaring a namespace other than `resolution` for the role observes that namespace on the rejected issue.
- [hard] REQ-03: Rejecting with a reason in a repository where no namespace declares the role fails with an error naming the missing `role = "rejection-reason"` declaration, and the issue's state, labels and event log are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: Rejecting with a reason where two or more namespaces declare the role fails naming each declaring namespace, and writes nothing.
- [hard] REQ-05: Rejecting without a reason behaves as before in a repository that declares no role.
- [hard] REQ-06: The `jit-default` profile's `resolution` entry and this repository's `.jit/config.toml` declare the role, so rejecting with a reason in either still records `resolution:<reason>`.
- [hard] REQ-07: No production source formats a `resolution:` label; the `--reason` help text and the reject documentation describe the label as recorded under the namespace declared for the role.
- [hard] REQ-08: The namespace role field is documented with the namespace declaration in the configuration reference.
- [hard] REQ-09: A lease refusal precedes the role check: rejecting with a reason an issue leased by another agent, in a repository declaring no role, fails with the lease refusal.

## Notes

- The reason value is still refused before any write when it cannot form a valid label value.
- Another in-flight effort changes field updates and readiness in `commands/issue.rs` and `commands/mod.rs`, and another edits `cli.rs` and the lease-enforcement CLI tests; whichever lands later rebases.
- `NamespaceConfig` is loaded by `JitConfig::load`, which another in-flight effort is changing. This work adds a field to the struct only and does not edit the loader; validation of role uniqueness happens at use time in the reject command, not in `config validate`.
- Serves `@/inv/domain-agnostic` and `@/inv/semantic-types`.

planning.outcome: issue reject --reason records under the declared rejection-reason namespace and refuses when none is declared

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One label constructor, one command and one config field change together with their tests and reference docs.

footprint.uncertainty: Paths that enumerate NamespaceConfig fields (profile application, namespace-registry schema, config schema output) are found when the field is added.

title: Expand the container criteria token from declared item-kind markers
description:
`{container.hard_criteria}` scans the container description for lines starting with the literal `[hard]`, so a repository declaring another criterion marker gets an empty expansion. The token must take its markers and sections from the repository's item-kind declarations.

## Background

- `extract_hard_criteria` (`crates/jit/src/templates.rs`) collects every list line in the whole description that starts with `[hard]`; `InterpolationContext` (same file) substitutes the result for `{container.hard_criteria}`.
- Item kinds declare `section`, `id-pattern` and `markers` under `[item_kinds.<kind>]`. The pure extraction in `crates/jit/src/domain/item.rs` (`index_items`, `ItemKind::markers`, `marker_matches`) already scans a kind's declared section and keeps entries matching its declared markers and id pattern.
- `expand_template` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template_expand.rs`) receives only documentation and hierarchy configuration; the template-apply path (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs`) already holds the captured item kinds.
- No shipped template uses the token today.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The token expands to the container's items of every issue-scope item kind that declares at least one marker, each extracted from that kind's declared section and kept when it carries one of that kind's markers, in description order.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test over a repository whose criterion kind declares a marker other than `[hard]` (for example `[must]`) expands the token to exactly the container's items carrying that marker.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test over a repository that declares no item kind with markers expands the token to an empty block.
- [hard] REQ-04: In this repository the token expands to the container's requirement items carrying `[hard]` or `[aspirational]`.
- [hard] REQ-05: No production source names a criterion marker; `extract_hard_criteria` and its literal scan are gone.

## Notes

- The token keeps its name; whether to rename it now that aspirational items are included is an open owner decision.
- A marked line without an id-pattern match is prose, not an item, and is not expanded.
- Other in-flight work adds a `{container.slug}` token to `InterpolationContext`, changes template-apply prerequisites in `template_expand.rs` and `commands/template.rs`, and edits gate presets reached from `commands/template.rs`; whichever lands later rebases.
- The template-apply test fixture expands the token in a harness that declares no marked item kind; it declares one or its expectation changes. This work does not change `TemplateRegistry::load`.
- Serves `@/inv/domain-agnostic` and `@/inv/convention-convergence` (one item-extraction path).

planning.outcome: The container criteria token expands from declared item-kind markers and sections

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One interpolation field changes its source to the existing item extraction, threading kinds through two callers.

title: Classify permanent links by the declared permanent paths
description:
The link validator treats `docs/`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `LICENSE` and `dev/architecture/` as permanent whatever the repository declares. Link permanence must follow the declared `permanent_paths`.

## Background

- `LinkValidator::is_permanent_path` (`crates/jit/src/document/link_validator.rs`) hardcodes the list; its only constructor is in `crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs` (`doc check-links`).
- `[documentation] permanent_paths` is the declared registry (`DocumentationConfig::permanent_paths`, `crates/jit/src/config.rs`); `ArtifactClassificationPolicy` (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_classifier.rs`) already normalizes it and matches paths against it.
- The `permanent_paths` rustdoc in `config.rs` scopes the paths to "inside the development root", which the link check does not require.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A root-relative link is classified permanent exactly when its path lies under a declared permanent path, using the existing normalized path matching.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test over a repository declaring a permanent path set that excludes `docs/` and includes another directory classifies a link into that directory as permanent and a link into `docs/` as not permanent.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test over a repository declaring no permanent paths classifies no root-relative link as permanent.
- [hard] REQ-04: No production source in the link validator names a documentation path.
- [hard] REQ-05: The `permanent_paths` rustdoc and the configuration reference describe both uses of the key: archival retention and link permanence.

## Notes

- This repository's link checks currently rely on `docs/` and root files being permanent. Declaring them in `.jit/config.toml` also affects archival classification; verify the archive plans of this repository are unchanged before declaring a path outside the development root, and otherwise leave the links reported as risky.
- Another in-flight effort unifies snapshot and link-check scopes in `commands/document.rs`; whichever lands later rebases. A backlog effort moves configuration reads onto captured declarations; read `permanent_paths` through whichever path exists when this lands.

planning.outcome: Link permanence follows the declared permanent paths alone

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One predicate swaps a literal list for an existing policy matcher, with its rustdoc and tests.

title: Suggest label fixes only with declared namespaces
description:
A malformed label without a namespace draws the suggestion `type:<label>` or `component:<label>`, whether or not the repository declares those namespaces. Suggestions must name only namespaces the repository declares.

## Background

- `suggest_label_fix` (`crates/jit/src/labels.rs`) hardcodes both namespaces for a colon-less label and never consults the registry; its dash-separator branch is unreachable because the colon-less case returns first.
- The message reaches users only through `validate_label_pattern`, called by label filter parsing in `crates/jit/src/cli.rs` (`IssueFilterArgs::parse`), `crates/jit/src/commands/query.rs` and `crates/jit/src/commands/search.rs`. Other `validate_label` callers discard the message.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A colon-less label's suggestion lists only namespaces declared in the repository's namespace registry.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test over a registry declaring namespaces other than `type` and `component` suggests those namespaces and neither of the two.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test over an empty registry reports the format error with no namespace suggestion.
- [hard] REQ-04: No production source in the label module names a namespace in a suggestion, and the unreachable branch is gone.

## Notes

- Label parsing in the CLI layer runs before configuration is loaded; the suggestion may move to the point where the registry is available, as long as the user still sees it on the same commands.
- Other in-flight work edits `cli.rs` command classification; whichever lands later rebases.
- A backlog effort moves configuration reads, including the namespace registry, onto captured declarations; read the registry through whichever path exists when this lands.

planning.outcome: Label-format suggestions name only declared namespaces

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure suggestion function gains a registry argument and its three callers pass it.

title: Answer the strategic query from declared strategic types alone
description:
`jit query strategic` falls back to every type at hierarchy level 1 or 2 when the repository declares no `strategic_types`. The query must return exactly the issues of declared strategic types and nothing when none is declared.

## Background

- `QueryOps::query_strategic` (`crates/jit/src/commands/query.rs`) builds the fallback from `level <= 2`; the pure `domain::queries::query_strategic` already returns an empty list for an empty type list.
- Existing CLI tests cover only taxonomies that declare `strategic_types`.
- The `query strategic` help in `crates/jit/src/cli.rs` and `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` describe it as reading "labels from strategic namespaces", which the code no longer does.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: With `strategic_types` declared, the query returns exactly the issues whose type is one of them; a test declares a set different from this repository's (for example a single non-epic type) and observes only its issues.
- [hard] REQ-02: With no `strategic_types` declared, the query returns an empty list; a test covers it.
- [hard] REQ-03: No production source in the query command names a hierarchy level.
- [hard] REQ-04: The command help and reference describe selection by declared strategic types.

## Notes

- Another backlog effort moves configuration reads onto captured declarations; use whichever read path exists when this lands.
- Other in-flight work edits command classification in `cli.rs`; whichever lands later rebases.

planning.outcome: query strategic returns declared strategic types only, empty when none declared

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Deleting one fallback branch plus two tests and two prose fixes is one short change.

title: Cluster the web graph on the declared strategic types
description:
The web graph clusters on hierarchy level 2, commented "typically epic", and derives its sub-cluster level by adding one. It must choose its cluster container from the strategic types the server serves, with no hierarchy-level literal in `web/src`.

## Background

- `assignNodesToSubgraphs` (`web/src/utils/subgraphClustering.ts`) picks `uniqueLevels.includes(2) ? 2 : uniqueLevels[0]`; comments in that file and `web/src/types/subgraphCluster.ts` name levels.
- `prepareClusteredGraphForReactFlow` (`web/src/utils/clusteredGraphLayout.ts`) takes the sub-container level as `primaryContainerLevel + 1`, assuming contiguous levels.
- `GraphView.tsx` fetches `GET /config/hierarchy` (`types`, `strategic_types`, `icons`) and drops `strategic_types`; the server already serves `[]` when none is declared.
- The module rustdoc of `crates/jit/src/graph/hierarchy.rs` describes the web as clustering at "the epic level (level 2)".

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The primary cluster container is the declared strategic type with the greatest served hierarchy level among types present in the graph; in this repository that yields epic clusters with milestones as visible nodes, as today.
- [hard] REQ-02: The sub-cluster level is the next declared hierarchy level after the container's, taken from the served level map rather than arithmetic.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test over a served hierarchy whose strategic types and levels differ from this repository's clusters on the declared type it selects.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test with no strategic types served renders the graph unclustered.
- [hard] REQ-05: `web/src` production code contains no hierarchy-level literal in code or comments, and the `graph/hierarchy.rs` rustdoc describes the web's selection by declared strategic types.

## Notes

- The served per-node `cluster` field names the topmost container (a milestone when one exists), so clustering on it would change this repository's view; it is not used here.
- Another backlog effort moves server configuration reads onto captured declarations; no server change is needed here.

planning.outcome: The web graph clusters on the served strategic types with no level literal

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two clustering utilities and one view switch from level literals to a served list.

title: Derive the snapshot README from its manifest
description:
The snapshot README is a static template that lists `docs/` and `dev/` as snapshot structure and claims complete configuration, whatever the export holds. It must describe only what that snapshot contains, derived from its manifest.

## Background

- `generate_readme` (`crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs`) interpolates two manifest counts into fixed prose: a `docs/` and `dev/` structure list (this repository's layout), "Complete JIT configuration and gate definitions", and a speculative "Import (Future)" section.
- `SnapshotManifest` (`crates/jit/src/snapshot.rs`) records `repo`, `scope`, issue files with state counts, document items with paths, hashes and assets, metadata and verification. Configuration files copied beside the issues are not recorded in it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The README's contents and structure sections list only what the manifest records: the issue files, the document paths (or their top-level directories) and the verification files.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test exporting documents under a directory other than `docs/` or `dev/` observes that directory in the README and neither `docs/` nor `dev/`.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test exporting a snapshot with no documents observes a README that names no documentation directory.
- [hard] REQ-04: The README carries no claim the manifest does not record, including complete configuration and future commands.

## Notes

- Another in-progress change rewrites the git access in the same file, and another in-flight change copies every declaration file into the snapshot; whichever lands later rebases. If declaration files become manifest entries, the README lists them through the same derivation.

planning.outcome: The snapshot README lists only manifest-recorded contents

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One README generator becomes a function of the manifest with two export tests.

title: Compare gate-registry edits and branch drift against the declared base branch
description:
The gate-registry guard and `jit validate --branch-drift` compare `HEAD` with the literal `origin/main`. Both must take their base from one repository declaration and skip, with a report, when none is declared.

## Background

- `require_common_history_with_main` (`crates/jit/src/commands/worktree.rs`) runs on gate define, update and remove (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs`) through `GitCheckout::compare_with_base("origin/main")`; it allows when git is absent, the base does not resolve, or histories are unrelated. Its rustdoc, error text and the gate.rs call-site comments name `origin/main` or "main".
- `validate_branch_drift` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs`) runs the same comparison on the write checkout and fails when the base does not resolve; `crates/jit/src/dispatch/validate.rs` maps it to a `branch_drift` check; `crates/jit/src/output/validate.rs` prints "Branch is up-to-date with origin/main"; the `--branch-drift` help in `crates/jit/src/cli.rs` names `origin/main`, as do the `--branch-drift` rows and drift prose in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` and `docs/reference/worktree-validate.md`.
- Both already run git against the invocation's repository, and whether the guard runs is decided by the worktree paths the caller supplies to the executor; no production source reads `JIT_TEST_MODE`.
- `[worktree]` (`WorktreeConfig`, `crates/jit/src/config.rs`) is adopter-authored; the `jit-default` profile leaves it to the adopter and lists it in its manifest comment.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `[worktree] base_branch` accepts a non-empty revision string other than `null`; the guard and the drift check compare against it.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test over a repository declaring a base other than `origin/main` (for example a local `trunk` branch) refuses a gate definition change on a diverged checkout, allows it on a checkout containing that base, and the drift check reports drift and up-to-date against that base.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test over a repository declaring no base: gate define, update and remove succeed and their output reports that the comparison was skipped because no base branch is declared; `validate --branch-drift` reports the `branch_drift` check as not run with the same reason and does not fail.
- [hard] REQ-04: Whether the guard runs stays decided by the inputs the caller sets on the executor; the change adds no environment, process working-directory or ambient read.
- [hard] REQ-05: The guard and drift surfaces describe comparison against the declared base and name no `origin/main` base: the guard's rustdoc and messages, the gate.rs call-site comments, the drift check's rustdoc and messages, the `--branch-drift` help, the drift output text, the `--branch-drift` rows and drift prose of the command and worktree-validate references, and the exit-code reference.
- [hard] REQ-06: This repository's `.jit/config.toml` declares `base_branch = "origin/main"` as repository-local policy; the shipped default profile declares none, and its adopter-left comment documents the key.

## Notes

- The comparison primitive `compare_with_base` stays base-agnostic in `storage/git.rs`.
- The shipped pre-commit hook and its documentation are a separate change that reads the same key.
- Other in-flight work changes lease checks, registry writes in gate define and gate presets in `commands/gate.rs`, and command classification in `cli.rs`; this change rebases onto them.
- `JitConfig::load` is being changed by another in-flight effort; adding the field to `WorktreeConfig` does not edit the loader. A backlog effort moves configuration reads onto captured declarations; read the key through whichever path exists when this lands.
- Serves `@/inv/domain-agnostic`, `@/inv/architecture-dependency-direction`, `@/charter/D-21` and `@/charter/D-4`.

planning.outcome: The gate-registry guard and branch-drift check compare against the declared base branch or report it undeclared

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two callers of one comparison primitive switch to one config key with shared skip reporting.

title: Check shared configuration commits against the declared base branch in the shipped hook
description:
The shipped pre-commit hook compares against `origin/main` or `main` and runs only when lease enforcement is on. It must read the repository's declared base branch and skip, with a notice, when none is declared, independent of lease mode.

## Background

- `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` (embedded by `crates/jit/src/commands/hooks.rs` and written by `jit hooks install`) reads `worktree.enforce_leases` through `jit config get`, skips with a warning when that call fails, exits when it is `off`, and then compares the merge base of `HEAD` with `origin/main`, falling back to `main`, when `.jit/config.toml` or `.jit/gates.toml` is staged.
- `jit config get` serves keys from `EffectiveConfig::full_snapshot` (`crates/jit/src/config.rs`), which lists `[worktree]` fields explicitly; a key missing from the snapshot exits 2 with "unknown config key", and a JSON `null` value prints `null` and exits 0.
- The `hooks install` help (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs`), the `hooks.rs` rustdoc and the hooks section of `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` say the hook "validates branch drift" or "branch divergence"; `scripts/hooks/README.md` and the "Git Hook Issues" section of `docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md` (including "Hook Not Running") name `origin/main` and tie the hook to enforcement mode.
- Repositories declare the base branch as `[worktree] base_branch`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The effective configuration always carries `worktree.base_branch`: `jit config get worktree.base_branch` prints the declared revision when declared, and prints `null` with exit status 0 when undeclared.
- [hard] REQ-02: With a shared configuration file staged and a declared base, the hook refuses the commit when the branch does not contain that base and allows it when it does; a test declares a base other than `origin/main` or `main`.
- [hard] REQ-03: With no declared base (`null`), the hook allows the commit and prints that no base branch is declared; a test covers it.
- [hard] REQ-04: When `jit` cannot be run, the hook prints that it could not read the configuration and allows the commit; a test runs the hook with no `jit` on `PATH`.
- [hard] REQ-05: The hook's base check runs whatever `worktree.enforce_leases` is set to.
- [hard] REQ-06: The hook script, its README, the `hooks install` help, the `hooks.rs` rustdoc, the hooks section of the command reference and the troubleshooting "Git Hook Issues" section describe what the hook checks, against the declared base; none names `origin/main` or `main` as the base or ties the check to enforcement mode.

## Notes

- `EffectiveConfig::full_snapshot` is part of another in-flight effort's configuration work; adding one key to its `worktree` object is the coordination point with that effort.
- Other in-flight work edits command classification in `cli.rs`; whichever lands later rebases.
- The hook still names the `.jit/` data root path; a relocated data root is outside this change.

planning.outcome: The shipped pre-commit hook compares against the declared base branch whatever the lease mode

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One shell script, its config read and its help prose change together with hook tests.

title: Record no worktree identity on an unborn branch instead of a fabricated main
description:
When `HEAD` names no commit, `jit init` records a worktree identity whose branch is `main`, a branch name no repository declared. Init must record no identity in that case, as it does outside git.

## Background

- `initialize_worktree_identity` (`crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs`) returns no identity when the checkout is not a git repository, but when the git head lookup yields nothing (an unborn branch) it falls back to the branch `"main"`; a unit test asserts `main` for an unborn `trunk` branch.
- `jit init --json` reports the identity's id as `repository_id` (`crates/jit/src/dispatch/init.rs`), and the command reference states that `repository_id` is `null` outside a git repository. The CLI test `test_init_json_reports_repository_id_inside_git` (`crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/init_tests.rs`) initializes git without a commit and expects a `wt:` id.
- Claims and `worktree info` already refuse a checkout with no commits (`GitRequirementGap::NoCommits` in `crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs` and `crates/jit/src/commands/worktree.rs`), and the identity is created on first use after a commit exists.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Initializing in a git checkout whose `HEAD` has no commit records no worktree identity, and `init --json` reports `repository_id: null`, exactly as initializing outside git does.
- [hard] REQ-02: Initializing on a named branch still records that branch, and a detached `HEAD` records what it records today.
- [hard] REQ-03: No production source supplies `main` as a branch value.
- [hard] REQ-04: The command reference states that `repository_id` is `null` outside a git repository and in a checkout with no commit.
- [hard] REQ-05: The CLI test of a `wt:` repository id commits before running init, so it still observes the id inside git.

## Notes

- The identity loader and its branch parameter are unchanged.
- The no-commit property is owned by the init unit test; the CLI test keeps owning the reported id for a checkout with a commit.

planning.outcome: Init records no worktree identity on an unborn branch rather than the literal main

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One fallback in one function becomes an early return with its unit test, one CLI test and one reference sentence.

footprint.uncertainty: Other CLI tests that initialize git without a commit and read the identity are found when the fallback is removed.
